# Quick reference: the R to Rust concept map {#sec-concept-map}

Every chapter from @sec-setup on ends with a summary table. This appendix collects the main pairings from those tables, grouped by part, with the chapter that covers each one. Treat them as starting points rather than equivalences: the chapters' "Where the analogy breaks" boxes say where each one stops working.

## Foundations

| R | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| Type at the console | Write `src/main.rs`, then `cargo run` | [-@sec-setup] |
| `x <- 5` | `let x = 5;`, or `let mut x = 5;` to allow reassignment | [-@sec-setup] |
| `function(x, y) x + y` | `fn add(x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 { x + y }` | [-@sec-setup] |
| `for (i in 1:3)` | `for i in 1..=3` | [-@sec-setup] |
| `c(10, 20, 30)` | `vec![10, 20, 30]` | [-@sec-vectors] |
| `x[1]` is the first element | `v[0]` is the first element | [-@sec-vectors] |
| `x[2:3]` copies two elements | `&v[1..3]`, a slice, copies nothing | [-@sec-vectors] |
| Recycling and vectorized arithmetic | A loop or an iterator | [-@sec-vectors] |
| `1L`, an integer, and `1`, a double | `1`, an `i32`, and `1.0`, an `f64` | [-@sec-types] |
| Types checked at runtime with `typeof()` | Types known at compile time | [-@sec-types] |
| Integer overflow gives `NA` and a warning | Panics in debug builds; wraps in release builds, except in division | [-@sec-types] |
| Mixed types are coerced automatically | Conversions are explicit, with `from()` or `as` | [-@sec-types] |
| `as.integer("x")` gives `NA` and a warning | `parse()` returns a `Result` | [-@sec-types] |
| A character vector | `String`, which owns text, and `&str`, which refers to it | [-@sec-strings] |
| `paste0()`, `sprintf()` | `format!` | [-@sec-strings] |
| `nchar()` | `chars().count()`; `len()` counts bytes | [-@sec-strings] |
| `NA` | `Option<T>`: `None` or `Some(value)` | [-@sec-missingness] |
| `if (!is.na(x))` | `if let Some(value) = x` | [-@sec-missingness] |
| `ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)` | `x.unwrap_or(0.0)` | [-@sec-missingness] |

## Objects and dispatch

| R | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| `list(mean = 0, sd = 1)` | `Normal { mean: 0.0, sd: 1.0 }`, after `struct Normal` | [-@sec-structs] |
| S4 slots | Struct fields with declared types | [-@sec-structs] |
| An S3 generic that calls `UseMethod()` | A method declared in a trait | [-@sec-s3-traits] |
| A method such as `variance.normal()` | `impl Distribution for Normal` | [-@sec-s3-traits] |
| A `.default` method | A default method in the trait, for its implementors only | [-@sec-s3-traits] |
| Class vectors and `NextMethod()` | No inheritance; traits and composition | [-@sec-s3-traits] |
| Any package can register any method | The orphan rule | [-@sec-s3-traits] |
| `print()` and `format()` methods, S4 `show()` | `impl fmt::Display` | [-@sec-display] |
| `str(x)` | `#[derive(Debug)]` and `{:?}` | [-@sec-display] |
| `sprintf("%.2f", x)` | `{:.2}` | [-@sec-display] |
| A validity function | A `new()` that returns a `Result` | [-@sec-s4] |
| `obj@sd <- -1` skips validity | Private fields can't be assigned outside their module | [-@sec-s4] |
| A virtual class | A trait | [-@sec-s4] |
| `"+.normal"`, `Ops.normal()` | `impl Add for Normal`, and the other operator traits | [-@sec-operators] |
| `setMethod("+", signature("Normal", "Uniform"))` | `impl Add<Uniform> for Normal` | [-@sec-multiple-dispatch] |
| Duck typing | A trait bound, `<T: Distribution>` | [-@sec-generics] |
| A list of objects of different classes | `Vec<Box<dyn Distribution>>` | [-@sec-generics] |
| `factor()` | An `enum` | [-@sec-enums] |
| `switch()` | `match`, which must cover every case | [-@sec-enums] |
| A list with a `family` tag | An enum variant with fields | [-@sec-enums] |
| `setClassUnion()`, which can gain members later | An enum, whose variants are fixed | [-@sec-enums] |
| S7 `new_class()` with a validator | A struct with private fields and a validating `new()` | [-@sec-s7] |

## Memory and mutation

| R | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| `y <- x` shares the value until one changes | `let y = x;` moves a `Vec` and copies a number; `.clone()` copies a `Vec` | [-@sec-ownership] |
| `tracemem()` finds the hidden copies | Copies are visible, usually as `.clone()` | [-@sec-ownership] |
| The garbage collector frees memory | Memory is freed when its owner goes out of scope | [-@sec-ownership] |
| A function that only reads its argument | `&T`, a shared reference | [-@sec-borrowing] |
| A function can't change its caller's vector | `&mut T`, a mutable reference | [-@sec-borrowing] |
| The garbage collector keeps referenced values alive | A reference can't outlive its value | [-@sec-borrowing] |
| An environment passed to a function and changed there | `&mut T` | [-@sec-environments] |
| A Reference Class | A struct with `&mut self` methods | [-@sec-environments] |
| Several names for one mutable object | `Rc<RefCell<T>>` | [-@sec-environments] |
| `on.exit()` | `impl Drop` | [-@sec-drop] |
| `reg.finalizer()` runs after a garbage collection | `drop()` runs at a known point in the code | [-@sec-drop] |

## Functions, errors, and macros

| R | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| `lapply(x, f)`, `sapply(x, f)` | `v.iter().map(f).collect()` | [-@sec-iterators] |
| `vapply(x, f, numeric(1))` | `.collect()` into a declared type | [-@sec-iterators] |
| `Filter(f, x)`, `x[x > 15]` | `.filter()` | [-@sec-iterators] |
| `Reduce(f, x, init)` | `.fold(init, ...)` | [-@sec-iterators] |
| `Map(f, x, y)` | `.zip()`, then `.map()` | [-@sec-iterators] |
| `\(x) x^2` | `|x: f64| x.powi(2)` | [-@sec-closures] |
| A function factory | A function that returns `impl Fn`, with `move` | [-@sec-closures] |
| Passing a function, as to `optimize()` | An argument of type `impl Fn(f64) -> f64` | [-@sec-closures] |
| `<<-` keeps state between calls | An `FnMut` closure | [-@sec-closures] |
| Arguments evaluated when first used | Arguments evaluated before the call; closures delay work | [-@sec-closures] |
| `stop()` | `Err(...)`, or `panic!` for bugs | [-@sec-errors] |
| `tryCatch()` | `match` on `Ok` and `Err`, or `?` to pass the error up | [-@sec-errors] |
| Condition classes | An error enum | [-@sec-errors] |
| `warning()` | `eprintln!`, or information in the result | [-@sec-errors] |
| `substitute()`, `quote()` | `macro_rules!`, expanded at compile time | [-@sec-macros] |
| `stopifnot()` | `assert!`, `assert_eq!` | [-@sec-macros] |
| `print()` while debugging | `dbg!` | [-@sec-macros] |

## Building Rust programs

| R | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| A named vector or list | `HashMap`, or `BTreeMap` for sorted keys | [-@sec-collections] |
| `table(x)` | `*counts.entry(v).or_insert(0) += 1` in a loop | [-@sec-collections] |
| `split(x, g)`, `tapply(x, g, f)` | `BTreeMap<K, Vec<V>>` with `entry().or_default().push()` | [-@sec-collections] |
| `unique()`, `union()`, `%in%` | `HashSet`, `BTreeSet` | [-@sec-collections] |
| A data frame | A `Vec` of structs, one per row | [-@sec-collections] |
| `readLines(path)` | `fs::read_to_string(path)?` and `.lines()` | [-@sec-io] |
| `read.csv()` | The `csv` crate, with `serde` structs | [-@sec-io] |
| `DESCRIPTION` | `Cargo.toml` | [-@sec-crates] |
| `export()` in `NAMESPACE` | `pub` | [-@sec-crates] |
| roxygen2 `#'` | `///` and `cargo doc` | [-@sec-crates] |
| `R CMD check` | `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo test` | [-@sec-crates] |
| `styler::style_pkg()` | `cargo fmt` | [-@sec-crates] |
| `Rscript` and `commandArgs()` | A compiled program, with `std::env::args()` or `clap` | [-@sec-cli] |
| `parallel::mclapply()` | `thread::spawn()`, `thread::scope()`, or `rayon` | [-@sec-concurrency] |
| `set.seed()` in each parallel task | A seeded generator per task, from `rand` | [-@sec-concurrency] |
| `unlist()` on a list of vectors | `.concat()` | [-@sec-concurrency] |
| `x[!is.na(x)]` | `v.iter().flatten().copied()`, then `.collect()` | [-@sec-capstone] |
| `sort(x)` for doubles | `v.sort_by(f64::total_cmp)` | [-@sec-capstone] |

## Extending R with Rust

| R and C | Rust | Ch. |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|----|
| `.Call("name", x)` | `#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn name` | [-@sec-extending-r] |
| `REAL(x)`, `INTEGER(x)` | The same functions, then `std::slice::from_raw_parts()` for a non-empty vector | [-@sec-extending-r] |
| `NA_INTEGER` | `i32::MIN` | [-@sec-extending-r] |
| C wrappers written by hand | `#[extendr]` and rextendr | [-@sec-extending-r] |
| A compiled objective for `optim()` | `rextendr::rust_function()` with `profile = "release"` | [-@sec-extending-r] |
